# Source: teambuilding notes (advanced)

**Do not edit this file.** It is a near-verbatim record of notes the user took
from masterclass videos by a Pokémon world champion, provided 2026-09-08. It
exists so that any later rewrite of the working reference files can be diffed
against what the source actually said.

Everything below this header is the source as written, including its own
spelling and shorthand. It is **generic VGC**, not Champions-specific: some
examples name Pokémon that are not in the Champions roster. Those are
corrected in the working files, never here. This file builds on the
foundational notes — read those first.

**Working files built on this:** `reference/archetypes.md`,
`reference/speed-control.md`, `reference/roles.md`,
`reference/team-evaluation.md`.

This file build off the Teambuildings file, read that first.

How to select a strong starting points?
--strong matchups
---can go for maximum good matchups OR making sure you always have some tools to win

Pokémon showdown has a great tool for lookup up pokemon for specific niches (e.g. a fast pokemon that learns a certain move)
--(is there a machine usable tool??? otherwise we need to think about this)

Inherent Strength vs Relative Strength
--Inherent Str
--- how good in a vacuum? 
--- Speed and Power generally the most important concepts
----can they move faster than others?
----can they do significant damage consistently?
--Relative Str
--- how good is a team in the current meta?
----a team can be inherently strong, but have low relative str
----unlikely that a team with low inherent str has high relative str, but is possible!

Types
--Some types are just better (e.g dragon vs bug)
---Some are better offensively, some defensively

Offensive Capabilities
-High SpA/Atk
-High Base power moves
-Neutral or SuperEffective htis
-Boosting items
-setup moves (e.g. sowrds dance, helping hand for patner, ect)
--boosting to +2 is the same as attacking twice, make sure you get value out of your setup
-Other Damge modifiers (weather, terrain, abilities, ect)

Offensive Coverage
-Type Coverage 
--dont over fixate! 
---sometimes youre just strong enough without supereffective
---resistances matter, but half of a big number can still be a big number
--you dont have to hit every single type for super effective damagem but if youre unable to hit certain key pokemon (meta threats) hard, itll be tough to knock out
-Physical and Special Coverage
-Base Damage of a move matters as much as type (i.e. icy wind is good for speed control, but not for damage, blizzard is better for that)
--Offensive moves should have at least 80 power in general, preferably at least 90
--Damage modifiers really matter!!!



Offensive Items
-Choice items - 1.5x damage or speed, but stuck in move
--dont run protect on a choice item mon, its usually a waste
--spread moves good
-Life orb
--recoil adds up, be wary
--some abilities ignore the life orb recoil
-Type boosting items (mystic water, charcoal, ect)
--very good on pokemon that run multiple moves of one type (i.e. aqua jet and wave crash)
--also good on pokemon that often jsut click one move (i.e. torkoal eruption)
-Most teams run  1-3 offensive items (FORMAT SPEIFIC, i.e. fewer items when megas are in)

Offensive Capabilities Distribution
-Focusing on just getting one pokemon set up can be successful, but prone to one mistake/crit hit effectively ending the game
--recommend more balance spread
--usually 1-2 support, the rest offensive/hybrid
--ALSO FORMAT SPEFICIC, in formats with restricted pokemon having just 1-2 damage deal restricted can be powerful
-Multiplicative scaling is important to keep in mind (i.e. STAB + Weather/Terrain bonus)
-More Offensive tools that are combined the stronger a pokemon is
-Combining multiple offensive threats that beat each others counters is very powerful

Defensive Capabilites
-Dont obsess over defense the best defense is a strong offense
-High SpD/Def
-Neutral or Not very Effective hits
-Defensive Items
-Other Damage reductions (weather, terrain, abilities, ect)


Defensive Coverage
-Type Coverage 
--No more than 2 pokemon of the same type on the same team
---some exception, but rare and for specific purpose
--focus on Defensive Type Synergy (e.g Aegeslash/Hydreigon resists all types in the game)
---the more your team wants to swap pokemon, the more important defensive synergy is
--Try to have one resistance to every type (rule of thumb, not mandatory)
---more than one to common foes
--dont over fixate! 
---resistances matter, but half of a big number can still be a big number
---resistances cannot make up for just bad stats

Defensive items
-Damage Reduction
--Focus sash
--assault vest (cannot run status moves)
--Supereffective reduce berries (Shuca,Chople,Occa, ect)
--Seeds (activate on terrain)
-Healing
--Sitrus Berry
---Often considered one of the best items
---can turn 2HKO into 3HKO with healing below 50%
--Leftovers
---more situational, have to activate 5times to out heal sitrus
---good with other passive healings

Other ways to reduce damage
-- Screens (Light Screen, Reflect, Aurora Veil)
-- SpA/Atk reducing moves
-- Intimidate
-- Other abilities (friend guard, multiscale, ect)
-- Set up moves

Format Specific Teambuilding
-Don't hesitate to consider specific counters if you keep losing to one pokemon
-there ARE counters to every pokemon, no matter how strong

Relative Strength
-the Meta matters, i.e. it doesn't really matter if our team has a physical psychic weakness, if no physical psychic mons are seeing use
-DONT just focus on your team, think about who your team will go against
-Which pokemon commonly run together, and why?
-Ladder AND Tournament results matter, and effect what people play often.

Stats/Damage Calculation re:Teambuilding
-You CAN win with just default 32/32/2 splits
--Having a polish state spread can help you win games though, and help against specific matchups
--WHERE the stats go matter (HP vs Def/SpD can change survival scenarios)
-Consider other scenarios your team i likely to be in (foe has been intimidated, certain weather/terrain is up, ect)
-dont hyperfixate, you dont wanna lose what makes a pokemon good (if we dump all stats into defense/HP on an offensive pokemon, its usually a waste)

Pokepaste
-Useful format for exporting teams into common tools

Important Format Knowledge
-Rough distributions of: Trick Room, Fake Out, Follow Me, Rage Powder, Wide Guard, Prankster
-Speed Tiers
-Power Level
-Common/Key Strategies
